source_text: A composition of a locally quasi-finite morphisms is locally quasi-finite.

We have seen this for quasi-DM morphisms in
Lemma <REF_0001>
and for locally finite type morphisms in
Lemma <REF_0002>.
Let <MATH_0001> and <MATH_0002>
be locally quasi-finite. Let <MATH_0003> be a field and let
<MATH_0004> be a morphism.
It suffices to show that <MATH_0005> is discrete. By
Lemma <REF_0003>
the morphisms <MATH_0006>
and <MATH_0007> are locally quasi-finite.
In particular we see that <MATH_0008> is
a quasi-DM algebraic stack, see
Lemma <REF_0004>.
By
Theorem <REF_0005>
we can find a scheme <MATH_0009> and a surjective, flat, locally finitely presented,
locally quasi-finite morphism <MATH_0010>. By
Lemma <REF_0006>
we see that <MATH_0011> is locally quasi-finite over <MATH_0012>, in particular
<MATH_0013> is discrete. The morphism
<MATH_0014> is
surjective, flat, and locally of finite presentation hence
<MATH_0015>
is surjective and open. Thus it suffices to show that
<MATH_0016> is discrete.
Note that <MATH_0017> is a disjoint union of spectra of Artinian local
<MATH_0018>-algebras <MATH_0019> with residue fields <MATH_0020>, see
Varieties, Lemma <REF_0007>.
Thus it suffices to show that each
<MATH_0021>
is discrete, which follows from the assumption that
<MATH_0022> is locally quasi-finite.
